mainTopic: When ביטול חמץ still works, the moldy loaf on פסח and following the last item (בתר בתרא), and the ברכה on בדיקת חמץ
overview: The גמרא first asks why we cannot simply do ביטול during the sixth hour of ערב פסח. It answers that once the רבנן forbid the חמץ, it is treated like a Torah prohibition and no longer belongs to the person, so he cannot nullify it. רב's ruling that קידושין made with חמץ from the sixth hour on is not valid supports this. A ברייתא seems to allow ביטול even on יום טוב, but רב אחא בר יעקב explains that it is about dough that has not yet become חמץ. Next, רב rules that a moldy loaf found on פסח is permitted. After a long back-and-forth about following the majority versus following the last item (בתר בתרא), רבה explains that רב means several days of eating מצה have passed. In that case even heavy mold could have formed on מצה. The גמרא then explains why a ברייתא about a coin box follows the majority rather than the last use. Finally, רב יהודה rules that one who does בדיקת חמץ must say a ברכה, and two versions of its wording are given in the name of רבא.

steps.title: Why not nullify the חמץ in the sixth hour?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why one cannot simply do ביטול during the sixth hour, when he burns the חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him nullify it in the sixth hour!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short, sharp question: why do we need to do ביטול earlier? Why not just do it in the sixth hour, when he is burning the חמץ anyway?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion said ביטול is done at the time of בדיקה, the night before. The challenge is that this seems unnecessary, since a person could just do ביטול later, at the time of ביעור. That would also cover any חמץ he found in the meantime.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullifying chametz: declaring it worthless and ownerless in one's heart
The sixth hour of the day on ערב פסח
Then let him nullify it (a challenge form)

phrases.english: But let him nullify it in the sixth [hour]!
phrases.notes: Meaning: at the time he burns the חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous discussion about when ביטול should be done.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of doing ביטול early, at the time of בדיקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ביטול could be done in the sixth hour, there would be no need to do it earlier.

steps.title: Rabbinic prohibition makes the חמץ no longer his
steps.stepSummary: Once the רבנן forbid the חמץ in the sixth hour, it is treated like Torah-forbidden חמץ. It is no longer his to nullify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since a rabbinic prohibition is on it, it is like a Torah prohibition. It is not in his possession, and he cannot nullify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that by the sixth hour it is too late, because the חמץ is already forbidden מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביטול works only on something a person owns, because he is giving up his ownership. Once the חמץ is forbidden for benefit, even only מדרבנן, the רבנן gave it the same force as a Torah prohibition. So it is considered as if it is not his, and his declaration does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the sixth hour is forbidden מדאורייתא. The Torah prohibition starts later. The point here is that even the rabbinic prohibition is enough to take the חמץ out of his ownership.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the ביטול formula is said before the prohibition begins, either at night after בדיקה or in the morning before the sixth hour.

phrases.english: Since a rabbinic prohibition is upon it,
it is like a Torah [prohibition],
and it does not stand in his possession,
and he is unable to nullify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Legal principle: a rabbinic prohibition has the force of a Torah prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the sixth hour is only rabbinically forbidden, the חמץ is still really his and can be nullified.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbinic prohibition takes the חמץ out of his ownership, so ביטול no longer works.

steps.title: Proof from betrothal with chametz after the sixth hour
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that קידושין done with חמץ from the sixth hour on is not valid. This shows the rabbinic prohibition makes the חמץ legally worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב גידל said in the name of רבי חייא בר יוסף, in the name of רב: one who betroths a woman from the sixth hour onward, even with hard mountain wheat, we are not concerned about the betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer: a ruling from רב about קידושין done with חמץ in the sixth hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין needs an object worth at least a פרוטה. Even though the sixth hour is only rabbinically forbidden, רב says the קידושין fails, because the חמץ counts as worthless. This shows that the רבנן treated rabbinic חמץ exactly like Torah-forbidden חמץ, which is the same idea as step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Hard wheat from the mountains, which is unlikely to become chametz

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how strongly the רבנן enforced their prohibition: strongly enough to cancel a קידושין that would otherwise be valid by Torah law.

phrases.english: As Rav Giddel said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Chiya bar Yosef said that Rav said:
One who betroths [with chametz] from six hours and onward,
even with hard mountain wheat,
phrases.notes: This wheat is very hard, so it is doubtful whether it became חמץ at all.

phrases.english: we are not concerned about the betrothal.
phrases.notes: The woman is not considered betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That rabbinic חמץ is treated like Torah-forbidden חמץ and is not considered his
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling, through רב גידל and רבי חייא בר יוסף, that קידושין with חמץ from the sixth hour on is not valid

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא: nullifying on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one may nullify חמץ in his heart even on יום טוב, which is after the prohibition has begun. This seems to contradict step 2.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that after the prohibition he cannot nullify it? But a ברייתא teaches: if he was sitting in the בית המדרש and remembered there is חמץ in his house, he nullifies it in his heart, whether on שבת or on יום טוב. Granted, you can find the שבת case: when the fourteenth falls on שבת. But יום טוב is already after the prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 2 by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא seems to allow ביטול after the חמץ is already forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שבת case is not a problem: if ערב פסח falls on שבת, he can nullify the חמץ in the morning, before the prohibition. But יום טוב of פסח is the fifteenth, long after the חמץ became forbidden. So the ברייתא seems to say ביטול works after the prohibition, which contradicts step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא?
He nullifies it in his heart
You can find such a case

steps.confusionAlert: The fourteenth of ניסן is never יום טוב. So the יום טוב in the ברייתא must be פסח itself, which is after the חמץ is already forbidden. That is the whole problem.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְבָתַר אִיסּוּרָא לָא מָצֵי מְבַטֵּיל לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And after the prohibition he cannot nullify it?
But wasn't it taught [in a baraita]:
If he was sitting in the study hall
and remembered that there is chametz in his house,
he nullifies it in his heart,
whether on Shabbat or on Yom Tov.
Granted, Shabbat, you can find such a case,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁחָל אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: for example, when the fourteenth falls on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: He remembers on Shabbat morning, before the prohibition begins.

phrases.english: But Yom Tov,
that is after the prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְבָתַר אִיסּוּרָא לָא מָצֵי מְבַטֵּיל לֵיהּ? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule established in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that ביטול cannot work after the prohibition begins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows ביטול on יום טוב, which can only be after the prohibition, so ביטול must work then.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about dough that is not yet חמץ
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב explains that the ברייתא is about a student who remembers kneaded dough at home that has not yet risen. He nullifies it before it becomes חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: here we are dealing with a student sitting before his teacher who remembers there is kneaded dough in his house and is afraid it will become חמץ. He acts first and nullifies it before it becomes חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא is not talking about real חמץ on יום טוב, but about dough that has not become חמץ yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, existing חמץ cannot be nullified. But dough that has not yet fermented is not forbidden yet, so it is still fully his. He nullifies it ahead of time, so that when it does become חמץ, it is already not his. The student cannot leave his teacher to go home, which explains why he relies on ביטול. The rule from step 2 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A student sitting before his teacher
He acts first, ahead of time

steps.whatToRemember: ביטול works only on something a person still owns. Once חמץ is forbidden, even מדרבנן in the sixth hour, it is too late. On יום טוב one can only nullify dough that has not yet become חמץ.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּתַלְמִיד יוֹשֵׁב לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹ עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a student sitting before his teacher,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִיסָּה מְגוּלְגֶּלֶת בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: and he remembered that there is kneaded dough in his house,
and he is afraid that it might become chametz.
He acts first and nullifies it before it becomes chametz.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: הָכָא בְּתַלְמִיד יוֹשֵׁב לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹ עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows nullifying existing חמץ on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about dough not yet fermented, which is nullified before it becomes forbidden.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ביטול after the prohibition does not work. On יום טוב one can only nullify dough before it becomes חמץ.

steps.title: The wording of the ברייתא supports רב אחא בר יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'sitting in the בית המדרש' shows that the dough has not yet become חמץ. This supports רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording also proves it. The ברייתא says: 'He was sitting in the study hall.' Learn from this that the explanation is correct.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב אחא בר יעקב's answer from Step 5, using the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the ברייתא mention that he was in the בית המדרש? It must be because he cannot get home in time to stop the dough from rising. That only makes sense if the dough has not yet become חמץ. So the ברייתא is about ביטול before the dough becomes חמץ, exactly as רב אחא בר יעקב said.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (it supports this explanation)
Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: ביטול on יום טוב works only for dough that has not yet become חמץ. Once the חמץ is forbidden, it is no longer his to nullify. This keeps the rule from Step 2 in place.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it teaches:
He was sitting in the study hall.
phrases.notes: He is away from home, so the dough may rise before he returns.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 5 from the ברייתא's own wording.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחא בר יעקב's claim that the ברייתא is about dough that has not yet become חמץ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's detail that he was sitting in the בית המדרש.

steps.title: A moldy loaf is permitted when most of the loaves are מצה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that moldy bread is permitted on פסח if there is more מצה than חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב: Bread that became moldy is permitted, as long as most of the loaves are מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב gives a ruling about a moldy loaf found among other loaves on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mold can be a sign that bread is old, so the loaf might be leftover חמץ from before פסח. רב says we may rely on the majority: if most of the loaves are מצה, the moldy loaf is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: There was more מצה (a majority of מצה)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Bread that became moldy,
once there is more matza, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated ruling begins after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A moldy loaf whose status is unclear is permitted on פסח when most of the loaves are מצה.

steps.title: What case is רב talking about? Not a loaf known to be חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact case. It rules out a loaf we know is חמץ, because a majority of מצה would not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he knows the loaf is חמץ, what difference does it make that most of the loaves are מצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to define the case in רב's ruling and rejects the first possibility. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A majority only helps when we are unsure. If we know this loaf is חמץ, the other loaves cannot change what it is. So רב cannot be speaking of a known חמץ loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (what are the circumstances)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying that a majority can permit real חמץ. The גמרא rejects that reading right here.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say that he knows it is leavened bread,
so what if there is more matza?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case רב's ruling in Step 7 is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation of the moldy loaf in רב's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It cannot be a loaf known to be חמץ. A majority of מצה does not change it.

steps.title: If the loaf's status is unknown, why do we need a majority of מצה?
steps.stepSummary: If we do not know whether the loaf is חמץ or מצה, we could follow the last bread placed there, even without a majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where we do not know if it is חמץ or מצה. But then why say 'when most is מצה'? Even without a majority of מצה, let us follow the last bread put there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second possibility, an unknown loaf. It then challenges why רב needed a majority at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During פסח, the most recent bread placed in the container would be מצה. If we follow the last item, the loaf should be treated as מצה even when the loaves are not mostly מצה. So mentioning a majority seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? (why mention this detail?)
Let us follow the last one (judge by the most recent item)

steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces 'following the last' as a way to decide doubts. It competes with the more familiar rule of following the majority.

phrases.english: Rather, where we do not know about it

phrases.aramaic: אִי חָמֵץ הוּא אִי מַצָּה הוּא —
phrases.english: whether it is leaven or whether it is matza,
why specifically when there is more matza?

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כִּי לֹא רָבְתָה מַצָּה נָמֵי,
phrases.english: Even when there is not more matza as well,
let us follow the last one.
phrases.notes: The last bread put there during פסח would be מצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second possible case after Step 8 rejected the first, then challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's condition that most of the loaves must be מצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a case of doubt, following the last item already makes the loaf מצה. So the majority condition seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A משנה about coins found in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה to support following the last: coins found by animal merchants are מעשר, while coins found on the הר הבית are חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did we not learn in a משנה: Coins found in front of animal merchants are always treated as מעשר. Coins found on the הר הבית are treated as חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up the idea of following the last, which it used in its challenge in Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People bought animals in ירושלים mostly with מעשר שני money, so coins near the merchants are treated as מעשר. Coins on the הר הבית are treated as חולין, even during a festival. The גמרא will explain in the next lines how this ruling shows that we follow the last.

keyTerms.meaning: Did we not learn in a משנה? (introducing a supporting source)
Here: מעשר שני money, which must be spent in ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is not changing the topic away from חמץ. It is quoted as a source for 'following the last,' which the גמרא will apply back to the moldy loaf.

phrases.english: Did we not learn in a mishna:
Coins that were found before animal merchants
are always tithe money.
On the Temple Mount, they are non-sacred.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא תְּנַן: מָעוֹת שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ לִפְנֵי סוֹחֲרֵי בְהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the principle 'follow the last' used in the challenge of Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The principle נֵיזִיל בָּתַר בָּתְרָא (following the last item).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about coins found near animal merchants and on the הר הבית.

steps.title: End of the משנה: coins found in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה finishes: coins found in ירושלים during the רגל are מעשר, and during the rest of the year they are חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ירושלים: if the coins are found during the festival, they are מעשר. If they are found during the rest of the year, they are חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the משנה it started in the last step. This last line is the part it actually needs for the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the רגל, crowds bring מעשר שני money to spend in ירושלים, so coins found then are probably מעשר. During the rest of the year this money is not common, so found coins are treated as חולין. The puzzle is why coins found even one day after the festival count as חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Pilgrimage festival, when everyone comes up to ירושלים
The rest of the days of the year

phrases.english: In Jerusalem, at the time of the festival: it is tithe money;
phrases.notes: Many pilgrims spend מעשר שני money then.

phrases.english: during the rest of the days of the year: it is non-sacred.
phrases.notes: This is the key line for the proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that we follow the most recent item placed in an area (the 'last'), even without a majority.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שקלים about coins found in ירושלים.

steps.title: The streets are swept daily, so found items are new
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה בר זירא explains that ירושלים's markets are cleaned every day, so any found coins are new. The גמרא applies this to the bread: the old loaves are gone, and this one is recent, meaning it is מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה בר זירא said: What is the reason? Since the markets of ירושלים are swept every day. So we see that we say: the earlier ones are gone, and these are new ones. Here too, let us say: the earlier bread is gone, and this loaf is from now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the משנה and then uses it as a proof for the moldy-bread case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coins dropped during the festival would have been swept up already, so coins found later must have been dropped recently. That shows we assume older items are gone and the item in front of us is the newest. The same logic would say the moldy loaf is new bread from פסח, so it is מצה, even without a majority of מצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the clearest source on the daf for the principle that the old items have been removed and we follow the newest one.

phrases.english: And Rav Shemaya bar Zeira said:
What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why are coins found right after the festival treated as non-sacred?

phrases.english: Since the markets of Jerusalem
are usually swept every day.
phrases.notes: So festival coins would already have been found.

phrases.english: So we see that we say:
the earlier ones are gone,
and these are other, newer ones.
Here too, let us say:
phrases.notes: Applying this to the moldy bread.

phrases.english: the earlier bread is gone,
and this one is from now.
phrases.notes: So it is מצה, not חמץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא אָמְרִינַן: קַמָּאֵי קַמָּאֵי אָזְלִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה and draws the proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: The claim from Step 9 that we follow the last bread placed there, so רב's need for a majority of מצה is hard to understand.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב שמעיה בר זירא's explanation of the משנה: the markets are swept daily.

steps.title: Mold shows the bread is old
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison: the bread is different, because its mold shows it has been sitting a long time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because its mold proves about it that it is old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the coin case does not fit the bread case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coins carry no sign of how long they have been lying there, so we can assume they are new. Moldy bread does carry a sign: mold takes time to grow, which suggests this is old bread from before פסח, meaning חמץ. So the rule that the earlier ones are gone does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Proves about it / testifies about it

phrases.english: It is different here,
because its mold proves about it.
phrases.notes: It proves the bread is old, and so likely חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the coins.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the coin principle to moldy bread, not the principle itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Moldy bread has a physical sign of age, and coins have none.

steps.title: If mold proves it, why does a majority help?
steps.stepSummary: If the mold proves the bread is old חמץ, then having more מצה around should not change anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its mold proves about it, then when there is more מצה, what difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer against רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If mold is a sign of חמץ, this particular loaf is shown to be חמץ. A majority of מצה in the house should not cancel that sign. So רב's condition of 'more מצה' seems pointless.

phrases.english: If its mold proves about it,
when there is more matza, what of it?
phrases.notes: The sign of mold should still win.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי עִיפּוּשָׁהּ מוֹכִיחַ עִילָּוָיהּ, כִּי רָבְתָה מַצָּה מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of Step 13 to challenge רב's ruling from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that moldy bread is permitted when there is more מצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If mold proves the loaf is חמץ, a majority of other bread cannot override that proof.

steps.title: רבה: 'more מצה' means many days of מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבה reinterprets רב: the point is not more מצה loaves, but that many days of eating מצה have passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Do not say 'there was more מצה.' Instead say: 'many days of מצה have passed over it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by changing how we read רב's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'More' refers to time, not quantity. After several days of פסח, the bread in the house has been מצה for a while, so mold could have grown on מצה too. The mold therefore no longer proves the loaf is from before פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say (read it this way)
Days of eating מצה, the days of פסח

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying there is a lot of מצה in the house. 'More' here means many DAYS have passed, not many loaves.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Do not say: 'that there was more matza,'
rather say:
'that many days of matza passed over it.'
phrases.notes: Enough time for מצה itself to become moldy.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא שֶׁרָבְתָה מַצָּה, אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording (לא תימא אלא אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'More מצה' meant a majority of מצה loaves, which cannot override the evidence of mold.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'More' means many days of פסח have passed, so the mold could be on מצה.

steps.title: Then it is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if many days of מצה passed, it is obvious the loaf is מצה. Why did רב need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's reading by saying it makes רב's ruling too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once days of פסח have passed and the old bread is presumed gone, there is little reason to suspect the loaf is חמץ. A teaching that obvious seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: If so, it is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's interpretation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If days of מצה have passed, permitting the loaf is obvious, so רב would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The case is heavy mold
steps.stepSummary: רב needed to teach the case where the mold is heavy. We might think heavy mold proves the bread is real old חמץ, so רב teaches that it is still permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where the mold is heavy. You might have said: since the mold is heavy, it is clear that it is certainly real חמץ. So רב teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge by naming a harder case that רב's ruling covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With light mold, permitting the loaf is obvious. With heavy mold, we might assume the bread is very old and certainly חמץ from before פסח. רב teaches that even heavy mold does not prove this once many days of מצה have passed, so the bread is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
He teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: רב permits moldy bread on פסח once many days of מצה have passed, even if the mold is heavy. The mold does not prove the bread is חמץ from before פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the final meaning of רב's ruling: it is about time passing, and it applies even to heavy mold.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where its mold is extensive.
You might have said:
since its mold is extensive,
the matter is revealed
that it is certainly real leavened bread;
so he teaches us that this is not so.
phrases.notes: Even heavy mold does not prove the loaf is חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing to a specific case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Heavy mold proves the bread is certainly old חמץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with heavy mold, after many days of מצה the bread is not assumed to be חמץ.

steps.title: Why heavy mold does not prove the bread is old
steps.stepSummary: Since many days of eating מצה passed, fresh hot מצה was placed on the loaf each day, and the heat made it mold faster.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since many days of מצה have passed over it, we say: every single day he baked hot bread and put it on top of this one, and that made it get moldier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind step 17: why heavy mold does not prove the bread is old חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every day of פסח, hot new מצה was put on top of the old loaf. The heat and moisture made it mold very fast. So heavy mold can form in a short time, and the loaf can still be from this פסח's מצה.

phrases.english: Since many days of matza have passed over it,
we say: each and every day
he baked hot bread,
and put it on top of it, and it grew moldier.
phrases.notes: The heat of the fresh bread speeds up the mold.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁרַבּוּ יְמֵי מַצָּה עִילָּוָיהּ, אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the answer in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual explanation of how the mold formed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Heavy mold proves the bread sat a long time, so it must be old חמץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hot מצה placed on it every day caused fast molding, so it can still be מצה.
steps.whatToRemember: Heavy mold on a loaf found after several days of פסח does not prove it is חמץ, because hot מצה placed on it every day makes it mold fast.

steps.title: Do we really follow the last use? The coin box
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges following the most recent use, citing רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who rules about a coin box by the majority of its use.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really follow the last one? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: a box that was used for regular coins and מעשר coins: if most were regular, the coins are regular; if most were מעשר, they are מעשר. Why? Let us follow the last use!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that we decide an item's status by its most recent use (בתר בתרא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 9 and 12 the גמרא assumed that we follow the last item placed somewhere (בתר בתרא). But רבי יוסי בר יהודה decides the coin box by majority (רוב), not by what was put in last. That suggests we do not follow the last item.

keyTerms.meaning: After the last one; following the most recent use
Coins of מעשר שני, which have holiness

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules: רוב means what was in the box most of the time, while בתר בתרא means what was in the box last.

phrases.english: And do we follow the last one?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
A box that was used for
non-sacred coins and tithe coins,
if mostly non-sacred, they are non-sacred;
if mostly tithe, they are tithe.
But why? Let us follow the last one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר בָּתְרָא? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back and challenges the principle of following the last item (בתר בתרא), which the גמרא assumed in step 9 and supported from the coins in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle of following the most recent use (בתר בתרא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא decides a mixed-use box by majority rather than by last use, so the last use should not decide the bread case either.

steps.title: Answer 1: He does not know which came last
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the ברייתא is a case where we do not know which kind of coin was put in last, so we cannot follow the last use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What case are we dealing with here? Where the box was used for regular coins and מעשר coins, and he does not know which one was last.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We would follow the last use if we knew what it was. In the ברייתא, nobody remembers which coins were put in last. So we fall back on majority. The rule of the last use stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowed case)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where it was used for
non-sacred coins and tithe coins,
and he does not know which of them was last.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא ignores the last use even when it is known.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is a case where the last use is unknown, so majority decides.

steps.title: Answer 2: Separate piles in one box
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד: the box held piles of both kinds of coins at the same time, so there is no clear last use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: It is a case where the box was used with piles and piles of coins.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives a second explanation of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both kinds of coins sat in the box at once, in separate piles. A coin could slide from one pile to the other. So there is no single last use to follow, and majority decides.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
For example, where it was used for piles and piles.
phrases.notes: Piles of each kind of coin in different parts of the box.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same קשיא as step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא rejects the last-use rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both kinds were in the box at once, so there is no last use.

steps.title: Answer 3: A coin found in a hole
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא: the coin was found in a hole in the box, so it may be left over from an earlier use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is a case where the coin was found in a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a third explanation of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coin stuck in a hole might have stayed there from long ago, when the other kind of coin was stored. So the last use does not tell us about this coin, and we follow majority.
steps.whatToRemember: All three אמוראים keep the rule of following the last use. They only explain why the coin-box case is different.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For example, where it was found in a hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא rejects the last-use rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: A coin in a hole may be old, so the last use does not apply to it.

steps.title: One who searches for חמץ must make a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: רב יהודה rules that a person doing בדיקת חמץ must recite a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: One who searches for חמץ must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the ברכה said over בדיקת חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא dealt with doubts about whether something is חמץ. Now רב יהודה teaches a new rule: the search itself is a מצוה that needs a ברכה before it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
One who searches must recite a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הַבּוֹדֵק צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever does בדיקת חמץ must say a ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the ברכה we say each year before בדיקת חמץ.

steps.title: Which words does he say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the exact wording of the ברכה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What ברכה does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact words of the ברכה. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said a ברכה is needed but not what it says. The question opens a discussion about wording.

phrases.english: What blessing does he recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of רב יהודה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of the ברכה on בדיקת חמץ.

steps.title: First version: ״לבער חמץ״
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי, in the name of רבא: the ברכה ends with ״לבער חמץ״, to remove חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: He says ״לבער חמץ״, to remove חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer gives the wording ״לבער חמץ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This wording uses the infinitive form, "to remove," like many ברכות on מצוות. It describes the act the person is about to do.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
He says: "to remove leaven."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.

steps.title: Second version: ״על ביעור חמץ״
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, also in the name of רבא: the ברכה is ״על ביעור חמץ״, concerning the removal of חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: ״על ביעור חמץ״, concerning the removal of חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report of רבא's view gives a different wording, ״על ביעור חמץ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רב פפי and רב פפא quote רבא, but they report different wordings. ״על ביעור״ is a noun form, "concerning the removal." The next step starts to examine what each wording implies.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
"Concerning the removal of leaven."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version of רבא's answer to the same question.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפי and רב פפא are two different people with similar names. Both quote רבא but give different wordings.

steps.title: Everyone agrees ״לבער״ means the future
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that everyone agrees ״לבער״ clearly refers to something about to be done.
steps.simpleTranslation: About ״לבער״, everyone agrees that it surely means the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the point both sides agree on. This sets up the next question: what does ״על ביעור״ imply?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברכה on a מצוה should be said before doing it. ״לבער״, "to remove," clearly points to an act about to happen, so it is acceptable to all. The open question is ״על ביעור״, which might sound like the act was already done.

phrases.english: Regarding "to remove":
everyone agrees
that it certainly implies the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the two wordings and starts with the point both sides accept.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״לבער״ clearly refers to the future, so all agree it works as a ברכה said before the מצוה.
